pl-l3d8c2-d1e117.summary: Asks whether Christ should be called twice begotten, as he is called Son of God and of man.

pl-l3d8c2-d1e120.summary: Answers that Christ was born twice and had two births.

pl-l3d8c2-d1e123.summary: Cites Augustine, De fide ad Petrum: God the Father begot from his nature the Son coequal and coeternal; the same only-begotten was born a second time, once from the Father, once from the mother; God the Word born of the Father, the Word made flesh born of the mother; one and the same Son born before the ages and in time, and both births, divine and human, belong to the one Son.
claims: The one Son was born of the Father and of the mother.
Both births belong to one Son.

pl-l3d8c2-d1e139.summary: Cites John Damascene: we venerate two births of Christ, one from the Father before the ages, beyond cause, reason, time, and nature; one in the last times, for us (for our salvation), like us (born a man from a woman in nine months), and above us (not from seed but from the Spirit and the Virgin, beyond the law of conception).
claims: Christ's eternal birth is beyond cause and time.
His temporal birth was for us, like us, and above us.

pl-l3d8c2-d1e148.summary: Concludes that Christ plainly has two births and is twice born.

pl-l3d8c2.summary: Asks whether Christ should be said to be twice begotten, as he is Son of God and of man. He was born twice and had two births: Augustine says the same only-begotten was born once of the Father and once of the mother, both births belonging to the one Son; Damascene venerates two births, one from the Father before the ages, beyond cause and time, the other in the last times, for us, like us, and above us.
claims: Both births belong to one Son.
The temporal birth was for us, like us, and above us.
